{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with multiple procedures",
      "quote": "1 (Day 1)",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Day 1 includes a large number of procedures: complete physical exam, neurological exam, ECOG PS, 12-lead ECG, vital signs, weight, cemiplimab infusion, hematology/chemistry, urinalysis, aPTT/INR, RF/ANA, TSH/CRP, ADA, PK, and concomitant medication review. This is a heavy burden for patients and may be logistically challenging for sites.",
      "fix": "Consider moving some non-critical assessments (e.g., RF/ANA, TSH/CRP) to a separate visit or to screening if not required at baseline."
    },
    {
      "title": "Redundant PK sampling on Day 1 and Day 22",
      "quote": "Cemiplimab PK/Drug Conc",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK samples are collected at every dosing visit (Day 1, 22, 43, 64) and at end of study. This is frequent and may be more than needed for a monoclonal antibody with a long half-life. Could reduce sampling to trough levels only.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting PK only at trough (pre-dose) on Day 22 and Day 43, and at end of study, to reduce patient burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight window for Day 22 and Day 43 visits",
      "quote": "22± 3 (Day 22)",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The ±3 day window for Day 22 and Day 43 visits is very tight, especially when combined with the need for PK, ADA, and imaging on the same day. This may lead to many schedule violations and require amendments.",
      "fix": "Widen the window to ±7 days for these visits, or separate efficacy imaging from dosing visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor biopsies at Day 22 may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor biopsies for Group 218",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a tumor biopsy at Day 22 (mid-treatment) is invasive and may be difficult to obtain, especially if the tumor is not easily accessible. This could lead to missing data and patient dropout.",
      "fix": "Consider making the on-treatment biopsy optional or allow collection at a more convenient time, such as at progression or end of treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "CT/MRI and/or digital photography at Day 22 and Day 43 may be redundant",
      "quote": "CT/MRI and/or digital photography",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Imaging is performed at Day 22 and Day 43, which is only 3 weeks apart. For a slow-growing cancer like BCC, this frequency may not be necessary and adds patient burden and cost.",
      "fix": "Consider imaging only at Day 43 and then every 12 weeks, unless clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sampling at Day 1 and Day 22 may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "ADA",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ADA is collected at Day 1 (baseline) and Day 22, but ADA responses typically take longer to develop. Sampling at Day 22 may be too early to detect treatment-emergent ADA, and could be moved to later timepoints.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting ADA only at Day 43 and end of study, with baseline at Day 1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Urine pregnancy test at end of study may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Urine Pregnancy Test",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The urine pregnancy test is listed at end of study, but if the patient has completed treatment and is no longer receiving study drug, this may not be required. It could be removed to reduce burden.",
      "fix": "Remove the end-of-study urine pregnancy test unless required by local regulations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Serum HCG at screening has a very short window",
      "quote": "Serum HCG ≤72 Hour Predose",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The serum HCG must be drawn within 72 hours before first dose, which is a very tight window and may cause delays in treatment if the result is not available in time. This is a common source of protocol deviations.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing a urine pregnancy test within 72 hours, or extend the window to 7 days with a confirmatory urine test on Day 1."
    }
  ]
}
